Back view muscle chart. Primary muscles: Triceps. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Abs.

svg.text: It loads the biceps from a fully straight arm to a hard squeeze on a bar you can add plates to, so arm work
progresses the same way the big lifts do.
Letting the elbows flare and travel forward — the movement becomes a shoulder press-down and the triceps stop being
Leaning your bodyweight over the bar to finish reps — the lats and chest push the stack down and the triceps get a
Stopping halfway back up — the triceps need the stretched position under tension, and short reps only train the
Grip the bar at chest height, elbows tucked to your ribs. Extend your arms
down until they are straight. Slowly return to the start without letting
Breathing — Exhale as you extend the arms down to a locked elbow and inhale as
the bar returns to chest height.
Coach's cue — Only your forearms move — keep the upper arms locked in place.
Set the pulley high and stand close enough that the cable pulls straight
down the line of your upper arm, so the elbow is not levered sideways.
Keep the elbows tucked and the load moderate — snapping into a hard lockout
against a heavy stack is a standard trigger for elbow tendinopathy.

Best on paper is not always best for you. Which exercise builds a body part fastest depends on your build, your injury history and how much of the movement you already own — someone who cannot yet hold

a flat back under load will get more from the exercise ranked third than from the one ranked first. Treat this as a starting point for a conversation, not a verdict: ask a coach on the floor before you
